{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement (Vendor: Cobalt Cloud)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Subject:** Verified playbook findings, walk-away items and recommended next steps

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. The document is strong in several important respects — the limitation of liability, assignment/change-of-control, audit, renewal, licence grant and insurance provisions all sit at our preferred position and require no redline — but it contains a cluster of serious, one-sided commitments running against us, plus two material omissions.

The most significant problems are:

- **No indemnity at all.** There is no Section 20 and no defence or hold-harmless obligation anywhere, even though Sections 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all cross-refer to indemnities that do not exist. We have inserted a Section 20 at the preferred position, with IP remedies numbered 20.5 to restore the 9.3 cross-reference.
- **Vendor owns everything we pay for.** Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable, with only a revocable, term-limited licence back to us — failing both our preferred and fallback positions.
- **A stack of Customer-only restrictive covenants.** Section 2.1 (three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights), Section 7.2 (Customer-side MFN/match obligation), and the two Section 12.4 provisions (24-month worldwide non-compete/exclusive dealing and a 24-month all-employee no-hire) each sit in walk-away territory. Each of these also directly contradicts Section 12.3, in which Vendor acknowledges we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, no-hire, minimum-volume or most-favoured-customer commitment, so deletion restores internal consistency as well as our commercial position.
- **No exit and no landing.** Section 9 provides no termination for convenience in a three-year term, and there is no post-termination transition-assistance or data-return obligation (Section 16.5 carves Customer Data out to a non-existent Section 11).
- **Governing law.** Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, which is outside our accepted list and conflicts with Section 28.2 (New York County).

One finding (performance warranty) is marked **needs review** and did not pass verification; we flag it below rather than treat it as concluded.

---

## 2. Findings table

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | No Section 20 (cross-refs at §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5; disclaimer at § 19.5) | No indemnity, defence or hold-harmless clause exists; new Section 20 inserted at preferred position with remedies at 20.5. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 14.2 | Vendor owns all Deliverables; licence back is revocable and term-limited. Redline reverses ownership, preserving Vendor Technology and the § 13.2 embedded-IP licence. |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Compliant | § 21.1 (with 21.2–21.4, 18.2, 1.5) | Mutual cap at greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, with our required carve-outs. No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Customer may assign to Affiliate or successor on notice; Vendor restricted. Favourable to us. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 (second) | Term-plus-24-month, all-territory exclusive dealing with no performance exit. Delete; confirm Vendor is non-exclusive. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages payable by Customer | Compliant | § 7.1 (with 7.3, 10.2, 21.1, 27.3) | No LDs, penalties or termination fees on us. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with 13.2–13.4) | Grant extends to Affiliates and contractors; perpetual paid-up licence to delivered software. No redline. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | 24-month post-term, unlimited scope and territory, sweeping in acquisitions and internal development. Delete; narrowed fallback offered in comment. |
| High | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 12.4 | One-way 24-month **no-hire** covering all Vendor employees, overriding general-advertising carve-outs. Delete; mutual 12-month fallback offered. |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Missing | § 9 (TERMINATION); cf. §§ 8.1, 2.1 | No convenience right in a three-year term. New § 9.4 inserted: 30 days' notice, pro-rata refund, overriding § 2.1. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with 22.2–22.3) | Once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, off-site where practicable, no system or unrelated-data access. No redline. |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 28.1 (cf. § 28.2) | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction; conflicts with § 28.2. Replace with New York law and New York County courts. |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | Deviation | § 7.2 | We must disclose and match any more favourable offer, with no product, time or comparison limits. Delete. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | Deviation | § 2.1 | Three-year USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights." Remove; pay for Services used or ordered (12-month reducible commitment with true-up as fallback). |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | § 8.2 | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, 60-day Vendor reminder, uplift capped at lesser of CPI and 3%. No redline. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 10.1 (cf. §§ 10.2, 16.5, 15) | No transition or data-return right; § 16.5 carves Customer Data out to a non-existent Section 11. New § 10.3 inserted (up to six months' assistance, machine-readable return within 30 days, certified deletion). |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | **Needs review (verification failed)** | § 19.1 (with 19.2–19.5, 6.2) | Reviewer's assessment is that §§ 19.1–19.5 sit at the preferred position and the automated period check failed only because the document spells out "ninety days". Verification did not pass, so we will confirm manually before signing off. No redline currently proposed. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with 18.2) | CGL 1M/2M, workers' comp, E&O 2M, cyber 5M, term plus one year. At preferred position. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

The following are identified in the findings as walk-away territory and should be treated as conditions of signature, not trading chips:

1. **§ 2.1 — Three-year, USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay with no reduction or termination rights** (MINCOMMIT).
2. **§ 7.2 — Open-ended Customer-side MFN/disclose-and-match obligation** (MFN).
3. **§ 12.4 — 24-month post-term, all-territory non-compete / exclusive dealing binding Customer** (NONCOMPETE and EXCLUSIVITY; the exclusivity finding addresses the separate acquire/develop covenant and is not double-counted).
4. **§ 12.4 — One-way 24-month no-hire covering all Vendor employees** (NOSOLICIT).
5. **Absence of any Vendor indemnity** — no Section 20, despite four cross-references presupposing one (INDEMN).
6. **Absence of any Customer termination for convenience in a three-year term**, compounded by § 2.1's express "no termination rights" language (T4C).
7. **§ 28.1 — Exclusive foreign (Singapore) governing law and venue**, which also conflicts with § 28.2 (GOVLAW).

Each of items 1–4 is contradicted on its face by Vendor's own acknowledgement in § 12.3, which we should put to Vendor directly.

---

## 4. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** implementing: deletion of §§ 2.1 (take-or-pay), 7.2 (MFN) and both § 12.4 covenants; reversal of Deliverable ownership in § 14.2 (preserving Vendor Technology and the § 13.2 embedded-IP licence); insertion of Section 20 (indemnification, with IP remedies at 20.5); insertion of § 9.4 (convenience termination on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund, overriding § 2.1); insertion of § 10.3 (transition assistance, 30-day machine-readable data return, certified deletion); and substitution of New York law and New York County courts in § 28.1.
2. **Lead the § 12.3 inconsistency argument** with Vendor: the covenants in §§ 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4 contradict Vendor's own acknowledgement that we have made no exclusivity, non-compete, no-hire, minimum-volume or MFC commitment. Alignment is a drafting fix as much as a commercial concession.
3. **Flag the broken cross-references** for Vendor to correct in the same turn: § 9.3 → "Section 20.5"; § 16.5 → "Sections 11 and 15" (there is no Section 11); § 28.1 versus § 28.2; and Section 23, which is a heading with no text.
4. **Complete manual verification of the WARRANTY finding (§§ 19.1–19.5)** before we close the review, since that item did not pass verification. Present position: no redline proposed.
5. **Offer the fallbacks where useful** to speed closure: a 12-month reducible minimum commitment with true-up (§ 2.1); a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to involved personnel with general-advertising carve-outs (§ 12.4); a narrowed, named-product non-compete for the term only with internal-development and acquisition carve-outs (§ 12.4); and 90 days' transition assistance with export within 30 days (§ 10.3).
6. **Confirm no further movement is needed** on §§ 7.1, 8.2, 13, 18, 21, 22 and 24, which we have cleared and should not be reopened."}
